_README: Copy this to watchlist.json in the repo root, then edit.
cp modules/watch/watchlist.example.json watchlist.json
watchlist.json is gitignored — your subjects of interest are not something
to publish to a remote. This example file is the only one that ships.
Each watch is one saved query against one connector. The runner keeps a
seen-set per watch and reports ONLY hits it has never seen, so a quiet
morning prints one line instead of yesterday's twelve results again.
backend: none | macos | file | ntfy
none    default. Nothing is sent anywhere.
macos   a local desktop notification. ZERO outbound traffic.
file    appended to evidence/watch/notifications.log.
ntfy    reaches your PHONE. This is the only backend that sends
anything off your machine — see the note below.
THE CONTENT RULE: a notification carries a COUNT and a WATCH ID.
Never a name, never a quote, never anything from a capture. The
notification is a doorbell, not a delivery — you open the desk to see
what arrived. notify.js enforces this and refuses a message that looks
like case content.
To use ntfy on your phone:
1. install the ntfy app (iOS App Store / Google Play / F-Droid)
2. pick a LONG, RANDOM topic name — anyone who guesses the topic can
read your notifications, so treat it like a password. Generate one:
openssl rand -hex 16
3. subscribe to that topic in the app
4. set backend to ntfy and paste the topic below
The ntfy.sh server sees every message you send through it. That is
survivable only because of the content rule above. Self-host with
"server" if you want even the counts to stay yours.
